summary: A complete target-level design of the dyadic unitary and symplectic ordinary lifting theorems of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni §§5–6: polarized deformation problems over a weight algebra at p = 2 with the classes µ_v, the dyadic dual Selmer group and its unavoidable class (OL.0); ordinary Hecke algebras of definite unitary groups at p = 2 with Hida control (OL.1); the ordinary global problem, its dimension bound, the Hecke-valued Galois representation and sufficiently deep levels (OL.2); Theorem 5.7.14 through solvable preparation, two-type patching, the component structure, Ihara-avoidance support and removal of the auxiliary place (OL.3); GSp₄ problems over a weight algebra, GSp₄-reasonable images with their Taylor–Wiles places, seed data, the selected problem and the Hida–Hecke Galois representation (OL.4); and Theorem 6.3.4 through component dominance and patching (OL.5). Generic deformation theory, local ordinary rings, patching algebra and the l-odd unitary theory are imported; nothing is claimed formalised.

nodes.title: Polarized deformation problems over a weight algebra, up to Ĝ_n-conjugacy
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ_2 be finite with ring of integers O, uniformizer ϖ and residue field k, and let CNL_O be the category of complete Noetherian local O-algebras with residue field k. Let F be an imaginary CM field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺, such that F/F⁺ is unramified at every finite place and every place of F⁺ above 2 splits in F. Let S be a finite set of places of F⁺ containing the set S_2 of places above 2 and the set S_∞ of infinite places, and write G_{F⁺,S} ⊃ G_{F,S} for the Galois groups of the maximal extension F(S) of F unramified outside S. Let 𝒢_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} be the group scheme of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7/clozel-harris-taylor-group, 𝒢_n^0 = GL_n × GL_1, ν : 𝒢_n → GL_1 its multiplier, and for A ∈ CNL_O let Ĝ_n(A) = ker(𝒢_n(A) → 𝒢_n(k)). Fix a continuous r̄ : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(k) with r̄^{−1}(𝒢_n^0(k)) = G_{F,S} whose restriction ρ̄ to G_{F,S} (projected to GL_n) is absolutely irreducible, and a continuous χ : G_{F⁺,S} → O^× lifting ν ∘ r̄ with χ(c_v) = −1 for every v ∈ S_∞. For each v ∈ S fix Λ_v ∈ CNL_O and put Λ = ⊗̂_{v∈S} Λ_v (completed tensor product over O). A lifting of r̄|G_{F⁺_v} to A ∈ CNL_{Λ_v} is a continuous r_v : G_{F⁺_v} → 𝒢_n(A) reducing to r̄|G_{F⁺_v} with ν ∘ r_v = χ|G_{F⁺_v}; the functor Lift^□_v of liftings is represented by R^□_v ∈ CNL_{Λ_v}. A local deformation problem D_v ⊂ Lift^□_v is a representable subfunctor stable under conjugation by Ĝ_n(A). A global deformation problem is a tuple 𝒮 = (F, r̄, O, χ, S, {Λ_v}_{v∈S}, {D_v}_{v∈S}). A lift of r̄ to A ∈ CNL_Λ is a continuous r : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(A) reducing to r̄ with ν ∘ r = χ; it is of type 𝒮 if r|G_{F⁺_v} ∈ D_v(A) for every v ∈ S; two lifts are strictly equivalent if they are conjugate by an element of Ĝ_n(A) (the whole kernel, including its GL_1 factor). For T ⊂ S, a T-framed lift of type 𝒮 is (r, (α_v)_{v∈T}) with α_v ∈ Ĝ_n(A), and (r, (α_v)) ~ (a r a^{−1}, (a α_v)) for a ∈ Ĝ_n(A). Def_𝒮 and Def^T_𝒮 : CNL_Λ → Set are the functors of strict equivalence classes of lifts (resp. T-framed lifts) of type 𝒮. When Λ_v = O for every v ∈ S ∖ T, R^loc_{𝒮,T} = ⊗̂_{v∈T} R_v (R_v representing D_v) is a Λ-algebra through ⊗̂_{v∈T} Λ_v ≅ Λ, and (r, (α_v)) ↦ (α_v^{−1} r|G_{F⁺_v} α_v)_v defines a CNL_Λ-morphism R^loc_{𝒮,T} → R^T_𝒮.
proofSteps: Define the functors as stated; Def_𝒮 and Def^T_𝒮 are represented by R_𝒮 and R^T_𝒮 in CNL_Λ (Thorne 2017, Lemmas 2.8 and 2.10, as BCGP §5.4 recalls them; the proofs use only that ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible and that the centralizer of r̄ in Ĝ_n is the image of the scalars, which holds for p = 2).
For T ≠ ∅, Def^T_𝒮 → Def_𝒮 is a torsor under (∏_{v∈T} Ĝ_n)/Ĝ_m, so R^T_𝒮 is formally smooth over R_𝒮 of relative dimension (n² + 1)#T − 1; for T = ∅, R^T_𝒮 = R_𝒮.

For v split in F as ṽṽ^c every lifting has image in 𝒢_n^0(A), and r_v ↦ ρ_v (projection to GL_n of r_v|G_{F_ṽ}) identifies liftings of r̄|G_{F⁺_v} with liftings of ρ̄|G_{F_ṽ}; Ĝ_n-conjugacy classes match GL_n-conjugacy classes there.
Coefficients over Λ are handled as in Khare–Thorne (2017, §4), which BCGP follow: the Λ-algebra structure plays no role in the tangent computations.
acceptance: For p = 2 and n even, Def_𝒮 differs from the functor of liftings up to 1 + M_n(m_A)-conjugacy, by the classes recorded in OL.0/dyadic-dual-selmer-group (µ_v).
The relative dimension of the framed ring over R_𝒮 is (n² + 1)#T − 1, not n²#T.

nodes.title: The classes µ_v and the dyadic dual Selmer group
nodes.statement: Keep the data of OL.0/lambda-polarized-deformation-problem with p = 2. Let ad r̄ = M_n(k) = Lie GL_n ⊂ 𝔤_n r̄ = Lie 𝒢_n with the adjoint action of G_{F⁺,S} through r̄, so that there is an exact sequence 0 → ad r̄ → 𝔤_n r̄ → k → 0. For v ∈ S identify Lift^□_v(k[ε]) with Z¹(F⁺_v, ad r̄), let L^1_v ⊂ Z¹ be the cocycles of D_v(k[ε]) and L_v its image in H¹(F⁺_v, ad r̄). Put µ_v = ker(H¹(F⁺_v, ad r̄) → H¹(F⁺_v, 𝔤_n r̄)) = im(H⁰(F⁺_v, k) → H¹(F⁺_v, ad r̄)). The trace pairing makes ad r̄(1) the Tate dual of ad r̄ (the twist is trivial since p = 2, but is kept in the notation). Let L_v^⊥ and µ_v^⊥ be the annihilators of L_v and µ_v. For T ⊂ S with Λ_v = O for v ∈ S ∖ T, the dual Selmer group is H¹_{𝒮^⊥,T} = ker(H¹(F(S)/F⁺, ad r̄(1)) → ∏_{v∈T} H¹(F⁺_v, ad r̄(1))/µ_v^⊥ × ∏_{v∈S∖T} H¹(F⁺_v, ad r̄(1))/L_v^⊥), and h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T} is its k-dimension. Properties: dim_k µ_v ≤ 1; µ_v ⊂ L_v; µ_v = 0 if v splits in F; µ_v has dimension one at an infinite place v at which (ρ̄, χ̄) is strongly residually odd; for T ≠ ∅ the cohomology h^i_{𝒮,T} of Thorne's complex C^•_{𝒮,T} vanishes for i ≠ 1, 2, h¹_{𝒮,T} = dim_k m_{R^T_𝒮}/(m_{R^loc}, m²) and h²_{𝒮,T} = h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T}.
proofSteps: The identification of µ_v with the image of H⁰(F⁺_v, k) comes from the long exact sequence of 0 → ad r̄ → 𝔤_n r̄ → k → 0; this gives dim µ_v ≤ 1, and µ_v = 0 when the sequence splits as G_{F⁺_v}-modules, that is when v splits in F (BCGP (5.4.2)).
µ_v ⊂ L_v because D_v is stable under Ĝ_n-conjugation; a cocycle in µ_v is the derivative of conjugation by an element (1, 1 + εa).
At an infinite place with (ρ̄, χ̄) strongly residually odd, µ_v is one-dimensional (Thorne 2017, Lemma 2.17(ii), as recalled by BCGP).

The vanishing of h^i_{𝒮,T} for i ≠ 1, 2 and h²_{𝒮,T} = h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T} is Thorne 2017, Lemma 2.15, via the Poitou–Tate sequence; µ_v^⊥ appears because H¹(F⁺_v, ad r̄)_η = im(H¹(F⁺_v, ad r̄) → H¹(F⁺_v, 𝔤_n r̄)) occurs in Thorne's long exact sequence and µ_v is the kernel (Remark 5.4.4).

Inflation–restriction compares H¹(F(S)/F⁺, ad r̄) with H¹(F(S)/F, ad r̄)^{Gal(F/F⁺)}: the kernel is the one-dimensional H¹(F/F⁺, k), whose localisation at v is µ_v, and restriction is surjective because H²(F/F⁺, k) injects into H²(F⁺_v, k) at a real place (Remark 5.4.4, with the corrected final term recorded in sourceIssues).
acceptance: If every finite place of T splits in F, then H¹_{𝒮^⊥,T} is the kernel of restriction to the infinite places at which L_v^⊥ = 0, together with no condition at T.
With T ≠ ∅, h²_{𝒮,T} = h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T}.

sources.match: Defines µ_v as the kernel of H¹ of ad r̄ into H¹ of 𝔤_n r̄, identifies it with the image of H⁰(F⁺_v, k), records dim ≤ 1, µ_v ⊂ L_v, vanishing at split places and the one-dimensionality at strongly residually odd real places, and defines the dual Selmer group with µ_v^⊥ at T and L_v^⊥ off T; quotes Thorne's vanishing and h² = h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T}.
Explains the role of µ_v (deformations equivalent under Ĝ_n but not under GL_n-conjugation) and compares with the conjugate self-dual Selmer groups by inflation–restriction.

nodes.title: Three forms of weak adequacy, and near adequacy
nodes.statement: Let k be a finite field, V a finite-dimensional k-vector space, ad = End_k(V), ad⁰ ⊂ ad the trace-zero endomorphisms and H ⊂ GL(V) a subgroup, with H^ss its set of semisimple elements. For g ∈ H^ss and α ∈ k̄ let e_{g,α} be the g-equivariant projection of V ⊗ k̄ onto the generalized α-eigenspace of g. The following are equivalent: (1) for every simple k[H]-submodule W ⊂ ad ⊗ k̄ there are σ ∈ H^ss and an eigenvalue α of σ with tr(e_{σ,α}W) ≠ 0; (2) the same for every simple k[H]-submodule W ⊂ ad⁰ ⊗ k̄; (3) ad is spanned over k by H^ss. They hold exactly when the trace-annihilator U = {w ∈ ad ⊗ k̄ : tr(gw) = 0 for all g ∈ H^ss} is zero; U = {w : tr(e_{g,α}w) = 0 for all g ∈ H^ss, α}; U is an H-submodule contained in ad⁰ ⊗ k̄. A subgroup satisfying them (weakly adequate) acts absolutely irreducibly on V. Consequently BCGP's nearly adequate subgroups (weakly adequate, H¹(H, k) = 0 and H¹(H, ad) = 0; Definition 5.3.3) are exactly the relaxed-adequate subgroups of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.4/relaxed-adequacy, and the Taylor–Wiles propositions recorded there apply to them.
proofSteps: Show the two descriptions of U agree: each e_{g,α} is a polynomial in g with coefficients in k̄, and conversely g = Σ_α α e_{g,α} for semisimple g (Thorne 2012, proof of Lemma A.1, as BCGP cite it).
U is H-stable: for h ∈ H, w ∈ U and g ∈ H^ss, tr(g·hwh^{−1}) = tr(h^{−1}gh·w) = 0 since h^{−1}gh ∈ H^ss.
Taking g = 1 shows U ⊂ ad⁰ ⊗ k̄. By non-degeneracy of the trace form, (3) ⇔ U = 0.
(1) and (2) say that U meets the socle of ad ⊗ k̄, respectively of ad⁰ ⊗ k̄, trivially; as U is an H-submodule of ad⁰ ⊗ k̄, each is equivalent to U = 0.

If H stabilizes a proper nonzero subspace V′, then every g ∈ H^ss stabilizes V′, so the span of H^ss lies in the parabolic subalgebra stabilizing V′ ≠ ad; hence (3) forces absolute irreducibility (after extending scalars the same argument applies over k̄).
Comparing definitions: PL.4/relaxed-adequacy requires H¹(H, k) = 0, H¹(H, ad) = 0 and condition (1); BCGP's Definition 5.3.3 requires weak adequacy (any of (1)–(3)), H¹(H, k) = 0 and H¹(H, ad) = 0.
acceptance: The trace-annihilator U always lies in ad⁰ ⊗ k̄.

Absolute irreducibility does not imply weak adequacy: GL₂(𝔽₂) ≅ S₃ acts absolutely irreducibly on 𝔽₂², but its semisimple elements are 1, A and A² with A of order 3, which span only the two-dimensional subalgebra 𝔽₂[A] ≅ 𝔽₄ of M₂(𝔽₂).
The group A₅ ⊂ GL₄(𝔽₂) of AbelianSurfacesModularity AM.2/a5-near-adequate is nearly adequate and not adequate in Thorne 2017's sense.

nodes.title: The unavoidable dyadic dual Selmer class
nodes.statement: Keep the data of OL.0/lambda-polarized-deformation-problem with p = 2, and let T = S ∖ S_∞. There is N₀, depending only on F⁺, such that for every N ≥ N₀ and every Taylor–Wiles datum (Q, (α_v)_{v∈Q}) of level N (each v ∈ Q outside S and split completely in F(ζ_{2^N}), ρ̄(Frob_v) semisimple with eigenvalue α_v; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.3/thorne-taylor-wiles-datum), h¹_{𝒮_Q^⊥,T} ≥ 1; in particular h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T} ≥ 1. Explicitly, let K⁺_m be the maximal totally real subfield of ℚ(ζ_{2^m}), choose m with K⁺_{m−1} ⊂ F⁺ and K⁺_m ⊄ F⁺, let L⁺ = F⁺K⁺_m (a totally real quadratic extension of F⁺) and let ψ ∈ H¹(F(S)/F⁺, ad r̄(1)) be the inflation of the nonzero class of H¹(L⁺/F⁺, k) through the scalars k ⊂ ad r̄. Then ψ ∈ H¹_{𝒮_Q^⊥,T} for every Taylor–Wiles datum of level N ≥ m.
proofSteps: ψ is trivial at every infinite place, because L⁺ is totally real, and at every v ∈ Q, because such v splits completely in F(ζ_{2^N}) ⊃ L⁺ for N ≥ m.

At a finite v ∈ S, let Δ_v be the image of H¹(F⁺_v, k) → H¹(F⁺_v, ad r̄). Then ψ_v ∈ Δ_v, and µ_v ⊂ Δ_v: µ_v is the image of the connecting map, whose cocycle vanishes on G_F and sends c ∉ G_F to the identity matrix (use the G_F-equivariant splitting 𝔤_n r̄ ≅ ad r̄ ⊕ k).
The Tate pairing on Δ_v × Δ_v is n times the pairing on H¹(F⁺_v, k) (the duality on ad r̄ is (X, Y) ↦ tr(XY) and tr(1_n) = n). If n is even it vanishes, so Δ_v ⊂ Δ_v^⊥ ⊂ µ_v^⊥ and ψ_v ∈ µ_v^⊥.

If n is odd, identify the pairing on H¹(F⁺_v, k) with the Hilbert symbol on F⁺_v^×/(F⁺_v^×)²; the classes are those of F/F⁺ and of L⁺/F⁺. The symbol is trivial at finite places prime to 2 (F/F⁺ is unramified there and L⁺/F⁺ is unramified outside 2), at infinite places (L⁺ is totally real) and at places above 2 (they split in F, so the class of F/F⁺ is locally trivial). Hence ψ_v ∈ µ_v^⊥ again.
acceptance: For n even, the scalar class of a totally real quadratic extension of F⁺ inside F(ζ_{2^∞}) survives every Taylor–Wiles datum of large level; so q = h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T} − 1 ≥ 0 in Proposition 5.5.6, and patching proceeds with one class left.
For F⁺ = ℚ one takes m = 3, K⁺_3 = ℚ(√2) and ψ the class of ℚ(√2)/ℚ.

Uses near adequacy to kill every class except a one-dimensional space: after adding Taylor–Wiles primes the remaining dual Selmer group injects into H¹(F_N/F⁺, k), which is two-dimensional, and the strongly residually odd real place cuts it to dimension one.

nodes.title: The universal ordinary Hecke algebra of a definite unitary group at p = 2
nodes.statement: Assume Hypothesis 5.7.1: F/F⁺ is unramified at every finite place, every place of F⁺ above 2 splits in F, and n[F⁺:ℚ] ≡ 0 mod 4. Let G/F⁺ be the definite unitary group of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.2/definite-unitary-group (quasi-split at every finite place, compact at infinity, with integral model and ι_ṽ : G(O_{F⁺_v}) ≅ GL_n(O_{F_ṽ}) at split v), with chosen ṽ | v for v | 2 and Ĩ_2 the embeddings F → E inducing these places. For λ ∈ (ℤ^n_+)^{Ĩ_2}, M_λ is the tensor product over τ ∈ Ĩ_2 of the O-lattices of highest weight λ_τ; for a set R ⊂ T ∖ S_2 of split places and characters χ_v : Iw(ṽ)/Iw_1(ṽ) ≅ (k(ṽ)^×)^n → O^× (v ∈ R), M_{λ,{χ_v}} = M_λ ⊗ ⊗_{v∈R} O(χ_v). For U = ∏U_v with U_v ⊂ ι_ṽ^{−1}Iw(ṽ) (v ∈ R), S_{λ,{χ_v}}(U, A) is the module of f : G(F⁺)∖G(𝔸^∞_{F⁺}) → M_{λ,{χ_v}} ⊗ A with f(gu) = u_{S_2∪R}^{−1}f(g). U is sufficiently small if its projection to some G(F⁺_v) has no nontrivial element of finite order. For 0 ≤ b ≤ c, U(l^{b,c}) replaces U_v (v | 2) by ι_ṽ^{−1}Iw(ṽ^{b,c}) (upper triangular mod ṽ^c, unipotent upper triangular mod ṽ^b). Hecke operators: T^j_w = ι_w^{−1}[GL_n(O_{F_w}) diag(ϖ_w 1_j, 1_{n−j}) GL_n(O_{F_w})] for split w ∉ T; U^j_{λ,ϖ_ṽ} = (w₀λ)(α^j_{ϖ_ṽ})^{−1}[U(l^{b,c}) ι_ṽ^{−1}(α^j_{ϖ_ṽ}) U(l^{b,c})] for v | 2; diamond operators ⟨u⟩, u ∈ T(O_{F⁺,2}). T^T_{λ,{χ_v}}(U(l^{b,c}), A) is the O-subalgebra of End_O generated by the T^j_w, (T^n_w)^{−1} and ⟨u⟩. Put Λ = O⟦T(l)⟧, where T(l) = ker(∏_{v|2} T(O_{F⁺_v}) → ∏_{v|2} T(k(v))) with T(k(v)) = (k(v)^×)^n. With U(l) = ∏_{v|2} ∏_j U^j_{λ,ϖ_ṽ} and e = lim_r U(l)^{r!}, T^{T,ord} = eT^T. Put S(U(l^∞), E/O) = colim_c S(U(l^{c,c}), E/O) and T(U(l^∞), O) = lim_c T(U(l^{c,c}), O). For λ = 0 the map T(l) → T^{T,ord}_{0,{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), O)^×, u ↦ (∏_{τ∈Ĩ_2} ∏_{i=1}^n τ(u_i)^{1−i})⟨u⟩, makes T^{T,ord}_{0,{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), O) a Λ-algebra; with this structure it is the universal ordinary Hecke algebra T^{T,ord}_{{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), O).
proofSteps: Specialize the constructions of PL.2/unitary-algebraic-modular-forms, PL.2/iwahori-ordinary-parts and PL.2/big-ordinary-hecke-algebra to l = 2. Those nodes are written for l odd; the definitions themselves do not use l odd, and Hypothesis 5.7.1 supplies the needed splitting of places above 2.

The operators T^j_w, U^j_{λ,ϖ_ṽ} and ⟨u⟩ commute with each other and with the inclusions S(U(l^{b,c}), O) ⊂ S(U(l^{b′,c′}), O) for b ≤ b′, c ≤ c′ (Geraghty, Lemma 2.10 of the published version, as BCGP cite it); the normalisation by (w₀λ)(α^j)^{−1} is what makes U^j act on integral forms.
The isomorphism T(U(l^∞), E/O) ≅ T(U(l^∞), O) of the limits is Geraghty, Lemma 2.17.
The twist ∏τ(u_i)^{1−i} is the character (w₀ν)^{−1} with ν_τ = (n − 1, …, 1, 0), as in PL.2/big-ordinary-hecke-algebra; it shifts the arithmetic primes so that weight λ corresponds to ℘_λ.
acceptance: The construction agrees with PL.2/big-ordinary-hecke-algebra word for word when 2 is replaced by an odd prime.
For n = 1 the twist is trivial and the twisted and untwisted Λ-structures coincide.

nodes.title: Hida theory for definite unitary groups at p = 2
nodes.statement: Keep OL.1/dyadic-ordinary-hecke-algebra with U sufficiently small (Definition 5.7.2) and U_v hyperspecial at split v ∉ T. Then: (1) T^{T,ord}_{{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), O) is a finite Λ-algebra, and it and all the finite-level Hecke algebras are reduced; (2) for each dominant λ and r ≥ 1, composing with the projection of M_λ onto its lowest weight line gives a Hecke-equivariant isomorphism S^{ord}_{λ,{χ_v}}(U(l^{r,r}), ϖ^{−r}O/O) ≅ S^{ord}_{0,{χ_v}}(U(l^{r,r}), ϖ^{−r}O/O) carrying U^j_λ to U^j_0 and twisting ⟨u⟩ by (w₀λ)(u); (3) the primes ℘_λ ⊂ Λ attached to dominant weights are Zariski dense in Spec Λ; (4) there is a natural identification Hom_O(T^{T,ord}_{0,{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), O)/℘_λ, ℚ̄₂) = Hom_O(T^{T,ord}_{λ,{χ_v}}(U(l^{1,1}), O), ℚ̄₂) (BCGP (5.7.4)).
proofSteps: Finiteness over Λ is Geraghty, Corollary 2.21 (published numbering), as BCGP cite it: when U(l^{b₀,b₀}) is sufficiently small, the Pontryagin dual of the ordinary forms is finite free over O⟦T(l^{b₀})⟧ (PL.2/ordinary-forms-free-over-lambda (b)), and Λ is finite over O⟦T(l^{b₀})⟧.
Reducedness is Geraghty, Lemma 2.14: S(U, ℚ̄₂) is a semisimple Hecke module, the T^j_w act semisimply, and the limit algebra embeds in a product of finite-level algebras.
Weight independence (2) is Geraghty's Proposition 2.6.1 (PL.2/hida-classicality (1)); its proof uses only the B_n(O)-equivariant projection to the lowest weight line and the normalisation of U^j.
Density of the ℘_λ is in the proof of Geraghty's Corollary 3.4; the identification (4) is Geraghty, Lemma 2.25 (PL.2/hida-classicality (3)).

BCGP use these statements at p = 2; the proofs require sufficient smallness of the level (ensuring exactness of S(U, −), PL.2/exactness-and-freeness) and the integrality of the normalised U-operators, and no hypothesis on the residue characteristic.
acceptance: Every O-algebra map T^{T,ord}(U(l^∞), O) → ℚ̄₂ above some ℘_λ comes from a classical ordinary form of weight λ and level U(l^{1,1}).
The finite Λ-algebra T^{T,ord}_m is a finite product of its localizations.

nodes.title: Ordinary algebraic modular forms at p = 2 and ordinary RACSDC representations
nodes.statement: Keep OL.1/dyadic-ordinary-hecke-algebra and fix ı : ℚ̄₂ ≅ ℂ. For λ ∈ (ℤ^n_+)^{Ĩ_2}, A_λ = colim_U S_λ(U, ℚ̄₂) is a semisimple admissible ℚ̄₂[G(𝔸^∞_{F⁺})]-module. The irreducible submodules of ıA_λ are the finite parts of the automorphic representations of G that are descents of automorphic representations π of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight λ (π has the infinitesimal character of the algebraic representation of weight λ, through ı); these π are isobaric sums of conjugate self-dual representations, and after localization at a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal only RACSDC π contribute. An irreducible submodule meets S^{ord}_λ(U(l^{b,b}), ℚ̄₂) for some b exactly when the corresponding π is ordinary, that is (ı^{−1}(⊗_{v|2} π_v))^{ord} ≠ 0.
proofSteps: Semisimplicity and admissibility of A_λ: G(F⁺ ⊗ ℝ) is compact, so A_λ ⊗_ı ℂ is a space of automorphic forms with finite-dimensional K-invariants and a positive-definite Petersson product.

Base change and descent between G and GL_n (Labesse, Corollaire 5.3 and Théorème 5.9, as BCGP cite them; PL.2/unitary-base-change-and-descent) identify the constituents with descents of weight-λ isobaric sums of conjugate self-dual representations.
At a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal the attached Galois representation is irreducible, which forces the base change to be cuspidal, so π is RACSDC (PL.2/unitary-base-change-and-descent (2)).

Ordinarity: the ordinary part at Iwahori level U(l^{b,b}) of ⊗_{v|2}π_v is nonzero exactly when π is ι-ordinary (BLGGT §2 as BCGP cite it; PA.2/iota-ordinary-automorphic-representation, PL.0/iota-ordinary-principal-series), which uses genericity of π_v at v | 2.
acceptance: Under the dictionary, a maximal ideal of T^{T,ord}_λ is non-Eisenstein exactly when the attached residual representation is absolutely irreducible, and then only ordinary RACSDC π of weight λ contribute.

nodes.title: The dyadic ordinary global deformation problem S_{χ} and R^{T,ord}
nodes.statement: Assume Hypothesis 5.7.1 and let π be an ordinary RACSDC automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) with ρ̄ = r̄_{π,2} : G_F → GL_n(k) absolutely irreducible (enlarging E as needed). By the dictionary of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7/clozel-harris-taylor-group and Thorne 2017 Lemma 2.2 (BCGP Lemma 5.1.2), ρ̄ extends to r̄ : G_{F⁺} → 𝒢_n(k) with ν ∘ r̄ = ε̄^{1−n}δ^n_{F/F⁺} and r̄^{−1}(𝒢_n^0(k)) = G_F, unique up to 𝒢_n^0(k)-conjugacy. Let T ⊃ S_2 be a finite set of finite places of F⁺ split in F, R ⊂ T ∖ S_2, and χ_v = (χ_{v,1}, …, χ_{v,n}) characters of O^×_{F_ṽ} trivial mod ϖ for v ∈ R; assume Hypothesis 5.7.5: T contains every finite place under a ramified place of π, and for v ∈ R, ρ̄|G_{F_ṽ} is trivial and π_ṽ^{Iw(ṽ)} ≠ 0. Put S = T ∪ S_∞, Λ_v = O for v ∉ S_2 and Λ_v = Λ_{GL_n,v} = O⟦I^{ab}_{F_ṽ}(2)^n⟧ for v ∈ S_2. The global problem is S_{χ} = (F, r̄, O, ε^{1−n}δ^n_{F/F⁺}, S, {Λ_v}, {D^{χ_v}_v}_{v∈R} ∪ {D^△_v}_{v∈S_2} ∪ {Lift^□_v}_{v∈S∖(R∪S_2)}), where D^{χ_v}_v is the problem of lifts with inertial characteristic polynomial ∏_j (X − χ_{v,j}(Art^{−1}σ)^{−1}) (LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2/ihara-avoidance-rings-p2 (3)) and D^△_v is Geraghty's ordinary problem (LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7/ordinary-flag-scheme over L8/ordinary-coefficient-ring). Local class field theory gives ⊗̂_{v∈S_2} Λ_v ≅ Λ, so R_{S_{χ}} and R^loc_{S_{χ},T} are Λ-algebras. For R = ∅ write S^{T,ord} = S_{χ} and R^{T,ord} = R_{S_{χ}} (Definition 5.7.11).
proofSteps: Extend ρ̄ to r̄ by the polarization of r̄_{π,2}; uniqueness up to 𝒢_n^0(k)-conjugacy is Thorne 2017 Lemma 2.2 (it holds in residue characteristic 2, unlike CHT Lemma 2.1.4).
Each local problem is Ĝ_n-stable and representable (LocalGaloisDeformationRings nodes), so S_{χ} is a global problem in the sense of OL.0/lambda-polarized-deformation-problem.
Identify Λ_{GL_n,v} = O⟦(O^×_{F_ṽ}(2))^n⟧ through Art_{F_ṽ}; the product over v | 2 is O⟦T(l)⟧ = Λ, the weight algebra of OL.1/dyadic-ordinary-hecke-algebra.

Since the χ_{v,j} are trivial modulo ϖ, D^{χ_v}_v and D^1_v agree on Artinian k-algebras killed by ϖ, which gives compatible isomorphisms R^loc_{S_{χ},T}/ϖ ≅ R^loc_{S_{1},T}/ϖ and R_{S_{χ}}/ϖ ≅ R_{S_{1}}/ϖ.
acceptance: For n even the multiplier is ε^{1−n}, since δ^n_{F/F⁺} = 1.

nodes.title: Every component of the ordinary deformation ring has dimension at least dim Λ
nodes.statement: In the setting of OL.2/ordinary-global-problem, every irreducible component of Spec R_{S_{χ}} has dimension at least dim Λ = 1 + n[F⁺:ℚ]. More precisely, R^loc_{S_{χ},T} is equidimensional of dimension 1 + n²#T + [F⁺:ℚ]n(n+1)/2, and there is a presentation R^loc_{S_{χ},T}⟦x_1, …, x_r⟧/(f_1, …, f_{r+s}) ≅ R_{S_{χ}} with s ≤ n²#T + [F⁺:ℚ]n(n−1)/2.
proofSteps: Local dimensions: R^{χ_v}_v has every component of dimension n² + 1 (R08.2/ihara-avoidance-rings-p2 (3)); R^□_v for v ∤ 2 is O-flat and equidimensional of dimension n² + 1 (Shotton, Theorem 2.5, as BCGP cite it; R08.2/fixed-type-rings-rank-n (1)); R^△_v is equidimensional of dimension 1 + n² + [F⁺_v:ℚ₂]n(n+1)/2 (L7/trivial-residual-flag-ring (5) when ρ̄|G_{F_ṽ} is trivial and [F⁺_v:ℚ₂] > n(n−1)/2 + 1; the general residual case is requested from LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7). Summing gives (5.7.8).

Presentation: a deformation–obstruction argument as in Clozel–Harris–Taylor Corollary 2.2.12 (GlobalGaloisDeformations G7/polarized-presentation), run with Thorne's complex C^•_{𝒮,T} so that it holds for p = 2 (OL.0/dyadic-dual-selmer-group), or Balaji's Proposition 4.2.5, gives the presentation with s ≤ n²#T + [F⁺:ℚ]n(n−1)/2.
Each component of a quotient of R^loc⟦x_1, …, x_r⟧ by r + s elements has dimension at least dim R^loc + r − (r + s) = 1 + [F⁺:ℚ]n.
acceptance: The bound is dim Λ = 1 + n[F⁺:ℚ], not 1 + n[F:ℚ] (the printed value; see sourceIssues).
Combined with finiteness over Λ, every component of Spec R_{S_{χ}} dominates a component of Spec Λ.

nodes.title: The Galois representation over the dyadic ordinary Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: In the setting of OL.2/ordinary-global-problem, suppose U_v is hyperspecial for every v ∉ T and U_v ⊂ ι_ṽ^{−1}Iw(ṽ) for v ∈ R. Then there is a maximal ideal m of T^{T,ord}_{{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), O) and a surjection of Λ-algebras R_{S_{χ}} → T^{T,ord}_{{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), O)_m. The corresponding representation r_m : G_{F⁺} → 𝒢_n(T^{T,ord}_{{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), O)_m), unique up to strict equivalence, is characterised by: for every finite place v ∉ T of F⁺ split as ww^c in F, r_m is unramified at w and w^c, and r_m(Frob_w) has characteristic polynomial X^n + ⋯ + (−1)^j q_w^{j(j−1)/2}T^j_w X^{n−j} + ⋯ + (−1)^n q_w^{n(n−1)/2}T^n_w.
proofSteps: Construct r_m as in Geraghty, Proposition 2.29 (published numbering; PL.2/ordinary-hecke-galois-representation (2)): glue the Galois representations of the ordinary constituents (OL.1/dyadic-ordinary-automorphic-dictionary) along the reduced finite-level Hecke algebras and pass to the limit.

The 𝒢_n-valued extension and its uniqueness up to strict equivalence use Thorne 2017 Lemma 2.4 in place of CHT Lemma 2.1.12, which needs residue characteristic > 2 (BCGP; compare Thorne 2017 Theorem 4.1).

The local condition at v | 2: r_m|G_{F_ṽ} factors through R^△_v, by Geraghty Corollary 3.4 (PL.2/ordinary-hecke-galois-representation (3)), checked on the dense set of classical points of OL.1/dyadic-hida-theory (3)–(4).
At v ∈ R the inertial characteristic polynomial is ∏_j (X − χ_{v,j}(Art^{−1}σ)^{−1}) (PL.2/ordinary-hecke-galois-representation (2)(iii)).
The map R_{S_{χ}} → T_m is surjective because T_m is generated by the T^j_w, which are coefficients of characteristic polynomials of r_m, and by the diamond operators, which are the image of Λ.
acceptance: The map is one of Λ-algebras for the twisted Λ-structure of OL.1/dyadic-ordinary-hecke-algebra.
A point of T_m above ℘_λ gives an ordinary RACSDC π′ of weight λ with r_{π′,2} the specialisation of r_m.

nodes.title: Uniform local fixed vectors for automorphic lifts of a residual representation
nodes.statement: Let w ∤ 2 be a finite place of the CM field F and π a RACSDC automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) with residual representation r̄_{π,2}. There is a compact open subgroup U_w ⊂ GL_n(O_{F_w}), depending only on r̄_{π,2}|G_{F_w}, such that every RACSDC automorphic representation π′ of GL_n(𝔸_F) with r̄_{π′,2} ≅ r̄_{π,2} satisfies (π′_w)^{U_w} ≠ 0.
proofSteps: By LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2/fixed-type-rings-rank-n (3) (BCGP Lemma 5.6.2), there is a finite F′_w/F_w over which every lift of r̄_{π,2}|G_{F_w} becomes unipotently ramified, and Spec R^□[1/2] has finitely many components.

Local–global compatibility at w (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.5/caraiani-upgrade-away-from-p-and-temperedness) identifies WD(r_{π′,2}|G_{F_w})^{F-ss} with rec(π′_w ⊗ |det|^{(1−n)/2}); π′_w is generic and tempered, so the lift r_{π′,2}|G_{F_w} is pure and lies on a single component, on which the restriction to inertia of the Weil–Deligne representation is constant (R08.2/fixed-type-rings-rank-n (2)). Hence only finitely many inertial types occur.

By the local Langlands correspondence these inertial types correspond to finitely many Bernstein components of GL_n(F_w) (requested from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.3), and each Bernstein component is generated by its vectors fixed by a suitable compact open subgroup (SR.3/bernstein-decomposition); take U_w to be the intersection of these subgroups.
BCGP's own proof uses the same finiteness together with the compatibility of the local Langlands correspondence with conductors; either route gives U_w depending only on r̄_{π,2}|G_{F_w}.
acceptance: U_w does not depend on π′, only on its residual representation at w.
The conductor of one lift does not bound the conductors of all lifts; uniformity is the content.

nodes.title: Sufficiently deep tame level
nodes.statement: In the setting of OL.2/ordinary-global-problem, let v ∈ T ∖ S_2 and ṽ | v the chosen place. A compact open subgroup U_v ⊂ G(F⁺_v) ≅ GL_n(F_ṽ) (via ι_ṽ) is sufficiently deep if it satisfies the conclusion of OL.2/uniform-fixed-vectors for w = ṽ: every RACSDC automorphic representation π′ of GL_n(𝔸_F) with r̄_{π′,2} ≅ ρ̄ has (π′_ṽ)^{U_v} ≠ 0. A level U is sufficiently deep at T if U_v is sufficiently deep for every v ∈ T ∖ S_2.
proofSteps: Sufficiently deep subgroups exist by OL.2/uniform-fixed-vectors.
If U′_v ⊂ U_v and U_v is sufficiently deep then so is U′_v, since (π′_ṽ)^{U_v} ⊂ (π′_ṽ)^{U′_v}.
acceptance: A sufficiently deep level sees every automorphic lift of ρ̄ that is unramified outside T and ordinary above 2, at the places of T ∖ S_2.

nodes.title: Solvable preparation and the auxiliary neat place
nodes.statement: Let F be a CM field, n ≥ 2, and ρ̄ : G_F → GL_n(𝔽̄₂) continuous, satisfying: (1) there is an ordinary RACSDC automorphic representation π of GL_n(𝔸_F) with r̄_{π,2} ≅ ρ̄; (2) F/F⁺ is unramified at every finite place, and every place of F⁺ above 2, and every place of F⁺ lying under a place at which π is ramified, splits in F; (3) n[F⁺:ℚ] ≡ 0 mod 4; (4) ρ̄(G_F) is nearly adequate (OL.0/weak-adequacy-equivalences); (5) ρ̄(G_F) contains a regular semisimple element; (6) if n is even, the polarized pair (ρ̄, ε^{1−n}δ^n_{F/F⁺}) is strongly residually odd at some infinite place of F⁺. Let T be a finite set of finite places of F⁺, all split in F, containing the places above 2 and the places under the ramification of π; let R^{T,ord} be the ring of OL.2/ordinary-global-problem (R = ∅), a Λ-algebra, and T^{T,ord}(U(l^∞))_m the localized universal ordinary Hecke algebra of OL.1/dyadic-ordinary-hecke-algebra with the map of OL.2/dyadic-hecke-galois-representation. Then there is a solvable CM extension F′/F, linearly disjoint from the field cut out by ρ̄ over F, such that, writing T′ for the places of F′⁺ above T and replacing E by a finite extension: hypotheses (1)–(6) hold over F′ with ρ̄(G_{F′}) = ρ̄(G_F); F′ = F′⁺(√−1); ρ̄|G_{F′_ṽ} is trivial for v ∈ T′; [F′⁺_v:ℚ₂] > n(n−1)/2 + 1 for v | 2; and for v ∈ T′ ∖ S_2, π_{F′,ṽ}^{Iw(ṽ)} ≠ 0, every lift of ρ̄|G_{F′_ṽ} is unipotently ramified, and if 2^N ∥ q_v − 1 then 2^N > n and O contains a primitive 2^N-th root of unity. Moreover there are infinitely many finite places v₁ ∉ T′ of F′⁺, split in F′, with ρ̄(Frob_{ṽ₁}) regular semisimple; for such v₁ and any torsion-free compact open U_{v₁}, every level U(l^{b,c}) with that factor is sufficiently small, and Hypotheses 5.7.1 and 5.7.5 hold for T′ ∪ {v₁}.
proofSteps: All conditions except F′ = F′⁺(√−1) are local; choose the local extensions (trivializing ρ̄|G_{F_ṽ} at T, raising local degrees above 2, making every lift at T ∖ S_2 unipotently ramified by LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2/fixed-type-rings-rank-n (3) — which also gives Iwahori-fixed vectors in π — and enlarging 2-power roots of unity) and realise them by a solvable CM extension linearly disjoint from F^{ker ρ̄} (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.0/auxiliary-cm-extensions); ordinarity and the RACSDC property are preserved by solvable base change (PA.2/iota-ordinary-soluble-base-change).

Adjoining √−1 is a quadratic extension; since a nearly adequate group has H¹(H, k) = 0, it has no normal subgroup of index 2, so ρ̄(G_{F′}) = ρ̄(G_F) and near adequacy, the regular semisimple element and strong residual oddness persist.

Hypothesis (5) and Chebotarev give infinitely many split v₁ with ρ̄(Frob_{ṽ₁}) regular semisimple. For p = 2 one cannot choose v₁ so that all deformations are unramified at v₁ (the usual choice for p > 2); instead every lift is a sum of characters at v₁ (R08.2/ihara-avoidance-rings-p2 (2)), which OL.3/sacrificial-prime-removal uses to remove v₁.
A torsion-free U_{v₁} makes every U(l^{b,c}) sufficiently small (Definition 5.7.2), which is what Geraghty's Lemma 2.6 requires (Remark 5.7.15).
acceptance: The extension does not change the residual image, so near adequacy is checked once over F.
The auxiliary place v₁ is chosen with regular semisimple residual Frobenius; this is where hypothesis (5) is used.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.7.14, first two paragraphs, and Remark 5.7.15, pp. 135–136
sources.match: Makes solvable CM base changes to arrange F = F⁺(√−1), trivial residual representation at T, large local degree above 2, Iwahori-fixed vectors and roots of unity at T ∖ S_2, keeping the image unchanged by near adequacy; then picks a split place v₁ with regular semisimple Frobenius and a torsion-free level there, so that the level is sufficiently small; explains that this replaces the p > 2 trick of an auxiliary place at which every deformation is unramified.

nodes.title: Patched modules for the unipotent and distinct-character problems
nodes.statement: In the situation produced by OL.3/neat-base-change-preparation, write T = S_2 ⊔ {v₁} ⊔ R, choose for v ∈ R pairwise distinct characters χ_{v,1}, …, χ_{v,n} of O^×_{F_ṽ} trivial mod ϖ, and let S_{1}, S_{χ} be the problems of OL.2/ordinary-global-problem. Take U_v = G(O_{F⁺_v}) at split v ∉ T, hyperspecial at inert v, U_v = Iw(ṽ) for v ∈ R, U_{v₁} torsion-free. Let m₁ ⊂ T^{T,ord}_{{1}}(U(l^∞), O) correspond to ρ̄ and m_χ the induced ideal (S^{ord}_{0,{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), k) = S^{ord}_{0,{1}}(U(l^∞), k)), and H_χ, H_1 the Pontryagin duals of the localized ordinary forms with E/O coefficients, so H_χ/ϖ ≅ H_1/ϖ. Put q = h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T} − 1, g = q + #T − 1 − [F⁺:ℚ]n(n−1)/2, S_∞ = Λ⟦X_1, …, X_{q+(n²+1)#T−1}⟧ with augmentation ideal a_∞, and R_{1,∞} = R^loc_{S_{1},T}⟦Y_1, …, Y_g⟧, R_{χ,∞} = R^loc_{S_{χ},T}⟦Y_1, …, Y_g⟧. The patching data are: CNL_Λ-maps S_∞ → R_{1,∞} and S_∞ → R_{χ,∞}; an R_{1,∞}-module H_{1,∞} and an R_{χ,∞}-module H_{χ,∞}, each finite free over S_∞; surjections R_{·,∞} ↠ R_{S_{·}} of R^loc-algebras factoring through R_{·,∞}/a_∞; isomorphisms H_{·,∞}/a_∞ ≅ H_{·} compatible with these surjections; and compatible identifications of all these data for 1 and χ modulo ϖ. Moreover dim R_{1,∞} = dim R_{χ,∞} = [F⁺:ℚ]n + (n²+1)#T + q = dim S_∞, so depth_{R_{·,∞}} H_{·,∞} = dim R_{·,∞} and the support of H_{·,∞} in Spec R_{·,∞} is a union of irreducible components.
proofSteps: Taylor–Wiles data: by Thorne 2017 Proposition 2.21 with adequacy relaxed to near adequacy (PL.3/taylor-wiles-primes-two-adic, PL.4/relaxed-adequacy; BCGP Proposition 5.5.6), for each N there are data (Q_N, (α_v)) of level N with #Q_N = q and R^loc_{S_{·},T}⟦X_1, …, X_g⟧ ↠ R^T_{S_{·,Q_N}}. The hypotheses (i)–(iv) of Proposition 5.5.6 hold: all liftings at the infinite places with χ(c_v) = −1, F = F⁺(√−1), strong residual oddness, near adequacy. One dual Selmer class always survives (OL.0/unavoidable-dual-selmer-class), whence q = h¹ − 1.

Auxiliary levels at Q_N with Δ_{Q_N} = ∏_{v∈Q_N} k(v)^×(2) acting by diamond operators (PL.3/taylor-wiles-level-structures specialized to 2); the Hecke modules at level Q_N are free over Λ[Δ_{Q_N}] by sufficient smallness (OL.1/dyadic-hida-theory), and the Galois representations over the Taylor–Wiles Hecke algebras come from OL.2/dyadic-hecke-galois-representation at level Q_N.

Patch as in Thorne 2012 Theorem 8.6 (the model of PL.3/ordinary-r-equals-t), using Proposition 5.5.6 in place of Thorne 2012 Proposition 4.4; the general patching statement is DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5/balanced-modules-and-module-patching with zero defect.
Dimensions: by OL.2/ordinary-dimension-bound (5.7.8), dim R_{·,∞} = 1 + n²#T + [F⁺:ℚ]n(n+1)/2 + g = [F⁺:ℚ]n + (n²+1)#T + q, which is dim S_∞ = dim Λ + q + (n²+1)#T − 1.

Since H_{·,∞} is finite free over S_∞, depth_{R_∞}H_∞ ≥ depth_{S_∞}H_∞ = dim S_∞ = dim R_∞, so H_∞ is maximal Cohen–Macaulay and its support is a union of components (Taylor 2008 Lemma 2.3; R03.6/nearly-faithful-and-component-support-conclusions, R03.5/kisin-patching-criterion).
acceptance: dim R_{1,∞} = dim R_{χ,∞} = dim S_∞.
The number of Taylor–Wiles variables is q = h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T} − 1, one fewer than for p odd.

nodes.title: Irreducible components of the patched deformation rings
nodes.statement: In the situation of OL.3/two-type-patching-data, for each minimal prime Q of Λ: (1) the generic points of R_{χ,∞}/Q and R_{1,∞}/Q have characteristic 0; (2) the irreducible components of Spec R_{χ,∞}/Q and of Spec R_{1,∞}/Q biject with products over v ∈ R ∪ {v₁} of irreducible components C_v of the corresponding local rings; (3) the irreducible components of Spec R_{χ,∞}/(Q, ϖ) = Spec R_{1,∞}/(Q, ϖ) biject with products over v ∈ R ∪ {v₁} of irreducible components C̄_v of the special fibres of the local rings; (4) the irreducible components of Spec R_{χ,∞}/Q biject with those of Spec R^□_{v₁}; (5) for each component C̄ = ⊗C̄_v of Spec R_{1,∞}/(Q, ϖ) there are components C_v of Spec R^1_v (v ∈ R) and components C^1_{v₁}, …, C^s_{v₁} of Spec R^□_{v₁} (s ≥ 1) such that the components of Spec R_{1,∞}/Q generalizing C̄ are exactly the C^i_{v₁} ⊗ ⊗_{v∈R} C_v.
proofSteps: Components of a completed tensor product of local rings whose components are geometrically irreducible and of characteristic 0 are products of local components, for the generic and special fibres (BLGHT11 Lemma 3.3 as used in Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne Lemma 3.2.4; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.4/completed-tensor-domains-and-components); power series variables do not change this.

Above 2, R^△_v/Q is geometrically irreducible with generically reduced special fibre (L7/trivial-residual-flag-ring (5), BCGP Proposition 5.6.6 (3)), so the places above 2 contribute a single component for each Q.

At v ∈ R, R^{χ_v}_v is irreducible with characteristic-0 generic point, and every prime of R^1_v minimal over ϖ contains a unique minimal prime (R08.2/ihara-avoidance-rings-p2 (3)); R^1_v/ϖ = R^{χ_v}_v/ϖ.

At v₁ the lifting ring has finitely many components, all of characteristic 0 (R08.2/fixed-type-rings-rank-n). Assemble (1)–(5) exactly as in Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne Lemma 3.2.4, using R03.6/completion-generic-special-components for the unique generalizations.
acceptance: Each generic point of the special fibre of R_{1,∞}/Q generalizes to components that differ only in their v₁-factor.

sources.match: States the five properties of the components of the patched rings modulo a minimal prime Q of Λ, deduced from Propositions 5.6.4 and 5.6.6 by the argument of [BCG+25, Lemma 3.2.4].

The model statement: equidimensionality of the completed local deformation ring, unique generalization of special-fibre generic points, bijection on components when the characters at R are distinct, and the comparison of special-fibre components; components of completed tensor products are products of local components.

nodes.title: Component support by Ihara avoidance and automorphic points on every local component
nodes.statement: In the situation of OL.3/two-type-patching-data: (a) for every set X of irreducible components C_v of Spec R^1_v (v ∈ R) there is an irreducible component C_{X,v₁} of Spec R^□_{v₁} such that C_{X,v₁} ⊗ ⊗_{v∈R} C_v lies in the support of H_{1,∞}; the corresponding quotient R^loc_X of R^loc_{S_{1},T} defines R_X = R_{S_{1}} ⊗_{R^loc_{S_{1},T}} R^loc_X, Spec R_X is contained in the support of H_1, (R_X)_red is a quotient of T^{T,ord}_{{1}}(U(l^∞), O)_{m₁}, and R_X is a finite Λ-algebra; (b) for every choice Y of irreducible components C_v of the local rings at v ∈ R ∪ S_2 there is an ordinary RACSDC automorphic representation π_Y of GL_n(𝔸_F) with r̄_{π_Y,2} ≅ ρ̄, r_{π_Y,2} unramified at every place not above T, and r_{π_Y,2}|G_{F_ṽ} lying on C_v and on no other component for each v ∈ R ∪ S_2.
proofSteps: The existence of π gives a nonempty support of H_{1,∞}; by the identification modulo ϖ the support of H_{χ,∞} is nonempty, and by (4) of OL.3/patched-component-structure it is a union of components of R_{χ,∞}/Q, each indexed by a component of R^□_{v₁}; by (5) and the mod-ϖ identification (Taylor's Ihara avoidance) every product C_{X,v₁} ⊗ ⊗C_v for a suitable C_{X,v₁} lies in the support of H_{1,∞}.

Then Spec R_X ⊂ Supp H_1, so (R_X)_red is a quotient of the Hecke algebra, which is finite over Λ (OL.1/dyadic-hida-theory); R_X is finite over Λ by topological Nakayama, since R_X/m_Λ is Noetherian of dimension 0 (R03.4/finiteness-of-deformation-rings-criteria).

By OL.2/ordinary-dimension-bound, Spec R_X → Spec Λ/Q is dominant for a minimal prime Q; choose a weight λ with R_X/℘_λ a nonzero finite O-algebra of dimension ≥ 1, which has a ℚ̄₂-point (R03.4/characteristic-zero-points-from-finiteness-and-dimension); it is a point of the Hecke algebra, hence (OL.1/dyadic-hida-theory (4), OL.1/dyadic-ordinary-automorphic-dictionary) comes from an ordinary RACSDC π_Y of weight λ.

Repeat for every minimal prime Q (which runs through the components at the places above 2). The local representations of π_Y lie on the prescribed components and on no other, by genericity of π_{Y,ṽ} (BLGGT Lemma 1.3.2(1); PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.1/generic-smooth-points).
acceptance: Every choice of local components at R ∪ S_2 is realised by an automorphic lift of ρ̄.

nodes.title: Removal of the auxiliary place by a second solvable base change
nodes.statement: In the situation of OL.3/ihara-avoidance-support, there is a solvable CM extension L/F, linearly disjoint from F^{ker ρ̄} over F, such that for every choice Y and every place w₁ of L⁺ above v₁, r_{π_Y,2}|G_{L_{w̃₁}} is unramified. Over L, with R′ the places of L⁺ above R, a split place v′₁ ∉ R′ ∪ S_2(L⁺) of L⁺ with ρ̄(Frob_{ṽ′₁}) regular semisimple, and T′ = S_2(L⁺) ∪ R′ ∪ {v′₁}, the patched module H′_{1,∞} for L has support containing every component C′_Y (the unramified component at v′₁ and the images of the components of Y elsewhere). Let R^loc_{L/F,T′} be the quotient of R^loc_{S_{1},T′} cut out by the union of the C′_Y and R′_{L/F,T′} = R′_{S_{1}} ⊗_{R^loc_{S_{1},T′}} R^loc_{L/F,T′}. Then Spec R′_{L/F,T′} lies in the support of H′_1, (R′_{L/F,T′})_red is a quotient of T^{T′,ord}_{{1}}(U(l^∞), O)_{m₁} over L, every O-point of R′_{L/F,T′} factors through this Hecke algebra, and R′_{L/F,T′} is a finite Λ′-algebra.
proofSteps: Every lift of ρ̄|G_{F_{ṽ₁}} is a direct sum of characters (ρ̄(Frob_{ṽ₁}) regular semisimple; R08.2/ihara-avoidance-rings-p2 (2), BCGP Lemma 5.6.3), so there is a finite extension of F_{ṽ₁} over which all lifts, in particular all r_{π_Y,2}, become unramified; realise it by a solvable CM L/F disjoint from F^{ker ρ̄} (PL.0/auxiliary-cm-extensions).
Repeat the patching of OL.3/two-type-patching-data over L with T′ = S_2(L⁺) ∪ R′ ∪ {v′₁} (the printed T′ omits S_2(L⁺); see sourceIssues).

The base changes of the π_Y (PA.2/iota-ordinary-soluble-base-change) show that each C′_Y is in the support of H′_{1,∞}, since a support that is a union of components containing a point lying on a single component contains that component.
Conclude as in OL.3/ihara-avoidance-support: the reduced quotient is a Hecke quotient, hence finite over Λ′.
acceptance: After the second base change no deformation condition at an auxiliary place is needed, because all relevant lifts are unramified there.

nodes.title: Finiteness of the dyadic ordinary deformation ring (Theorem 5.7.14, first part)
nodes.statement: Let F be a CM field, n ≥ 2, and ρ̄ : G_F → GL_n(𝔽̄₂) continuous, satisfying: (1) there is an ordinary RACSDC automorphic representation π of GL_n(𝔸_F) with r̄_{π,2} ≅ ρ̄; (2) F/F⁺ is unramified at every finite place, and every place of F⁺ above 2, and every place of F⁺ lying under a place at which π is ramified, splits in F; (3) n[F⁺:ℚ] ≡ 0 mod 4; (4) ρ̄(G_F) is nearly adequate (OL.0/weak-adequacy-equivalences); (5) ρ̄(G_F) contains a regular semisimple element; (6) if n is even, the polarized pair (ρ̄, ε^{1−n}δ^n_{F/F⁺}) is strongly residually odd at some infinite place of F⁺. Let T be a finite set of finite places of F⁺, all split in F, containing the places above 2 and the places under the ramification of π; let R^{T,ord} be the ring of OL.2/ordinary-global-problem (R = ∅), a Λ-algebra, and T^{T,ord}(U(l^∞))_m the localized universal ordinary Hecke algebra of OL.1/dyadic-ordinary-hecke-algebra with the map of OL.2/dyadic-hecke-galois-representation. Then R^{T,ord} is a finite Λ-algebra.
proofSteps: Prepare F′ (OL.3/neat-base-change-preparation), patch over F′, and remove the auxiliary place over a further solvable L (OL.3/sacrificial-prime-removal), so that R′_{L/F,T′} is finite over Λ′.

Restriction to G_L defines a commutative square Λ′ → R′_{L/F,T′} → R^{T,ord} over Λ′ → Λ. The restriction of a lift of type S^{T,ord} lies on the union of the C′_Y: above v′₁ it is unramified (v′₁ lies outside T), above 2 it is ordinary, and at the places of R′ it is unipotently ramified because F′ was chosen so that every lift of ρ̄|G_{F_ṽ}, v ∈ T ∖ S_2, becomes unipotently ramified over F′ (BCGP Lemma 5.6.2; this condition is left implicit in the source, see sourceIssues). The map R′_{L/F,T′} → R^{T,ord} is finite: this is BLGGT Lemma 1.2.3(1) for p = 2, whose proof is unchanged once CHT Lemma 2.1.12 is replaced by Thorne 2017 Lemma 2.4 (compare GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.4/restriction-finiteness).
Hence R^{T,ord} is finite over Λ′ and so over Λ (R03.4/finiteness-of-deformation-rings-criteria).
acceptance: Finiteness holds with no level hypothesis at T ∖ S_2.
It is the input BCGP Proposition 7.5.10 uses at p = 2, through the finite map R^{T,ord} → R_S of GSp₄ deformation rings.

nodes.title: The dyadic ordinary reduced R = T theorem (Theorem 5.7.14)
nodes.statement: Let F be a CM field, n ≥ 2, and ρ̄ : G_F → GL_n(𝔽̄₂) continuous, satisfying: (1) there is an ordinary RACSDC automorphic representation π of GL_n(𝔸_F) with r̄_{π,2} ≅ ρ̄; (2) F/F⁺ is unramified at every finite place, and every place of F⁺ above 2, and every place of F⁺ lying under a place at which π is ramified, splits in F; (3) n[F⁺:ℚ] ≡ 0 mod 4; (4) ρ̄(G_F) is nearly adequate (OL.0/weak-adequacy-equivalences); (5) ρ̄(G_F) contains a regular semisimple element; (6) if n is even, the polarized pair (ρ̄, ε^{1−n}δ^n_{F/F⁺}) is strongly residually odd at some infinite place of F⁺. Let T be a finite set of finite places of F⁺, all split in F, containing the places above 2 and the places under the ramification of π; let R^{T,ord} be the ring of OL.2/ordinary-global-problem (R = ∅), a Λ-algebra, and T^{T,ord}(U(l^∞))_m the localized universal ordinary Hecke algebra of OL.1/dyadic-ordinary-hecke-algebra with the map of OL.2/dyadic-hecke-galois-representation. If moreover U_v is sufficiently deep (OL.2/sufficiently-deep-level) for every v ∈ T ∖ S_2, then the surjection R^{T,ord} → T^{T,ord}(U(l^∞))_m of OL.2/dyadic-hecke-galois-representation has nilpotent kernel, so (R^{T,ord})_red ≅ T^{T,ord}(U(l^∞))_m.
proofSteps: By OL.3/dyadic-ordinary-finiteness and OL.2/ordinary-dimension-bound every component of Spec R^{T,ord} dominates a component of Spec Λ; hence the ℚ̄₂-points above the primes ℘_λ (dense in Spec Λ by OL.1/dyadic-hida-theory (3)) are dense in Spec R^{T,ord}.

Each such point is automorphic: its restriction to G_L is a point of R′_{L/F,T′}, which factors through the Hecke algebra over L (OL.3/sacrificial-prime-removal), so it is the Galois representation of an ordinary RACSDC representation over L by (5.7.4); by solvable descent (PL.0/soluble-descent) it is automorphic over F.
Since U_v is sufficiently deep for v ∈ T ∖ S_2, the corresponding automorphic representation has nonzero fixed vectors at level U(l^{1,1}), so by (5.7.4) the point lies in Spec T^{T,ord}(U(l^∞))_m.

A closed subset of Spec R^{T,ord} containing a dense set of points is everything; so the kernel of R^{T,ord} → T_m is contained in every prime, hence nilpotent (R03.6/faithful-quotient-ring-identification).
acceptance: Without the depth hypothesis the theorem still gives finiteness, but automorphic points may need a smaller level than U.
Downstream, Proposition 7.5.10 uses only the components through the point q of interest (see the corrected statement recorded for its proof).

nodes.title: GSp₄ deformation problems over a weight algebra and the framing ring
nodes.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real, p a prime, O, k as before, S_p the places above p, and ρ̄ : G_{F⁺} → GSp₄(k) continuous and absolutely irreducible with similitude ν ∘ ρ̄ = ε̄^{−1}. Write ad ρ̄ = 𝔤𝔰𝔭₄ (dimension 11) and ad⁰ρ̄ = 𝔰𝔭₄ (dimension 10) with the adjoint action. Let S ⊃ S_p be a finite set of finite places containing those where ρ̄ ramifies; for v ∈ S fix Λ_v ∈ CNL_O and put Λ = ⊗̂_{v∈S} Λ_v. A lift of ρ̄|G_{F⁺_v} to A ∈ CNL_{Λ_v} is a continuous ρ : G_{F⁺_v} → GSp₄(A) reducing to ρ̄ with ν ∘ ρ = ε^{−1}; the lifting functor D^□_v is represented by R^□_v, and D^□_v(k[ε]) ≅ Z¹(F⁺_v, ad⁰ρ̄), two liftings being ĜSp₄(k[ε])-conjugate iff their images in H¹(F⁺_v, ad ρ̄) agree. A local deformation problem is a subfunctor D_v represented by a quotient R_v of R^□_v and stable under ĜSp₄(A) = ker(GSp₄(A) → GSp₄(k)). A global problem is 𝒮 = (ρ̄, S, {Λ_v}, {D_v}); lifts ρ : G_{F⁺,S} → GSp₄(A), A ∈ CNL_Λ, with ν ∘ ρ = ε^{−1} are of type 𝒮 if every ρ|G_{F⁺_v} ∈ D_v(A); strict equivalence is ĜSp₄(A)-conjugacy; T-framed lifts (ρ, (γ_v)_{v∈T}) are taken up to (aρa^{−1}, (aγ_v)). D_𝒮 and D^T_𝒮 are represented by R_𝒮 and R^T_𝒮. For T ≠ ∅, D^T_𝒮 → D_𝒮 is a torsor under (∏_{v∈T} ĜSp₄)/Ĝ_m, R^T_𝒮 is formally smooth over R_𝒮 of relative dimension 11#T − 1, and with the framing ring 𝒯 = Λ⟦x_1, …, x_{11#T−1}⟧ (the coordinate ring of (∏_{v∈T}ĜSp₄)/Ĝ_m over Λ) a choice of representative ρ_𝒮 of the universal deformation gives R^T_𝒮 ≅ R_𝒮 ⊗̂_Λ 𝒯. When Λ_v = O off T, R^loc_{𝒮,T} = ⊗̂_{v∈T} R_v maps to R^T_𝒮.
proofSteps: Local representability is LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1/g-valued-framed-ring with fixed multiplier; the description of D^□_v(k[ε]) by 1-cocycles is ρ(σ) = (1 + εφ(σ))ρ̄(σ).
Global representability of D_𝒮 uses absolute irreducibility of ρ̄ (the centralizer of the image in ĜSp₄ is Ĝ_m), as for GL_n in GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.3/global-deformation-type.
The torsor statement and R^T_𝒮 ≅ R_𝒮 ⊗̂_Λ 𝒯 follow as in R04.2/framed-unframed-comparison, with dim ĜSp₄ = 11 and the diagonal Ĝ_m acting trivially.
acceptance: The global representations have domain G_{F⁺} (the source writes G_F in Definition 6.1.4; see sourceIssues).
For #T = 1 the framing ring has 10 variables.

nodes.title: GSp₄-reasonable residual representations
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 3, k a finite field of characteristic p, F a number field and ρ̄ : G_F → GSp₄(k) continuous and absolutely GSp₄-irreducible (its image lies in no proper parabolic subgroup of GSp₄ over k̄; this is a standing assumption of Whitmore §3). Let 𝔰𝔭₄ = Lie(Sp₄) ⊗ k (the Lie algebra of the derived group of GSp₄) with the adjoint action of GSp₄(k), 𝔰𝔭₄^∨ its dual, and for a semisimple h ∈ GSp₄(k) let 𝔷_h = Lie Z(Z_{GSp₄}(h)) ∩ 𝔰𝔭₄ be the Lie algebra of the centre of the centralizer of h, intersected with 𝔰𝔭₄. A subgroup H ⊂ GSp₄(k) satisfies the reasonableness conditions if (a) H⁰(H, 𝔰𝔭₄^∨) = 0 and (b) for every nonzero simple k[H]-submodule W ⊂ 𝔰𝔭₄^∨ there are a semisimple h ∈ H, w ∈ W and z ∈ 𝔷_h with w(z) ≠ 0. ρ̄ is GSp₄-reasonable if for all sufficiently large n the group H_n = ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^n})}) satisfies (a) and (b), and, when ζ_p lies in the field cut out by 𝔰𝔭₄^∨ (equivalently by ad⁰ρ̄), also H¹(H_n, 𝔰𝔭₄^∨) = 0. (This is Whitmore's Ĝ-reasonable for Ĝ = GSp₄; version 4 of Whitmore's preprint renames the notion.)
proofSteps: State the conditions for subgroups first and then for ρ̄ through the tower F(ζ_{p^n}); for p > 2 the trace form identifies 𝔰𝔭₄^∨ with 𝔰𝔭₄ equivariantly.

If H¹(ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}), k) = 0 the groups H_n are independent of n (a normal subgroup of p-power index would give a nonzero homomorphism to ℤ/p), so the conditions can be checked on H_1 (Whitmore Lemma 3.20).
For h regular semisimple, Z_{GSp₄}(h) is a maximal torus, so 𝔷_h is the Cartan subalgebra of 𝔰𝔭₄ through h; condition (b) then says that W does not vanish on that Cartan subalgebra.
acceptance: Vast implies GSp₄-reasonable.
A ρ̄ with image in the diagonal torus is not GSp₄-reasonable.

nodes.title: Taylor–Wiles data for GSp₄-reasonable residual representations
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 3, 𝒮 = (ρ̄, S, {Λ_v}, {D_v}) a GSp₄ problem (OL.4/gsp4-lambda-deformation-problem) over a totally real F⁺, T ⊂ S with S_p ⊂ T, and n ≥ 1. Suppose ρ̄(G_{F⁺(ζ_{p^n})}) satisfies condition (b) of OL.4/gsp4-reasonable and, if ζ_p lies in the field cut out by 𝔰𝔭₄^∨, H¹(ρ̄(G_{F⁺(ζ_{p^n})}), 𝔰𝔭₄^∨) = 0. Let q ≥ h¹(G_{F⁺,S}, 𝔰𝔭₄^∨(1)). Then there is a set Q of Whitmore Taylor–Wiles places of level n (places v ∉ S with q_v ≡ 1 mod p^n at which ρ̄ is unramified with semisimple Frobenius ḡ_v, with Whitmore's local condition D^TW_v attached to the Levi subgroup centralizing ḡ_v) with #Q = q and H¹_{𝒮_Q^⊥,T}(𝔰𝔭₄^∨(1)) = 0.
proofSteps: By Whitmore's local analysis (requested from LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2), the dual Selmer condition at a Taylor–Wiles place v is H¹_ur(F_v, N_v^∨(1)), with N_v = Lie Z(M_{ḡ_v}) ∩ 𝔰𝔭₄; a class [ψ] is killed by adding v exactly when it has nonzero image in H¹_ur(F_v, N_v^∨(1)) (Whitmore Lemma 3.14).
Induct on the dimension: it suffices, for each nonzero [ψ] ∈ H¹(G_{F⁺,S}, 𝔰𝔭₄^∨(1)), to find infinitely many such places.

Let L be the field cut out by 𝔰𝔭₄^∨(1) and L_n = L(ζ_{p^n}). By Whitmore Lemma 3.16 (BCGP21 Lemma 7.5.9; ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7/gsp4-big-image-verification), H¹(Gal(L_n/F⁺), 𝔰𝔭₄^∨(1)) = 0 under the hypotheses, so ψ restricts to a nonzero G_{F⁺(ζ_{p^n})}-equivariant homomorphism f : G_{L_n} → 𝔰𝔭₄^∨(1).

Take a simple submodule W of the span of f(G_{L_n}); condition (b) gives semisimple σ₀ and z ∈ 𝔷_{σ₀} with w(z) ≠ 0 for some w ∈ W; adjust σ₀ by τ ∈ G_{L_n} with ψ(τ) = w if needed, so that ψ(σ)(z) ≠ 0 for σ = τσ₀ with ρ̄(σ) = ρ̄(σ₀).
Chebotarev gives infinitely many places v with ρ̄(Frob_v) = ρ̄(σ), ψ(Frob_v) = ψ(σ) and Frob_v ∈ G_{F⁺(ζ_{p^n})}.
acceptance: The Frobenius at a Taylor–Wiles place need only be semisimple, not regular semisimple; this is what allows reasonable rather than vast images.
For #Q = q = h¹(G_{F⁺,S}, 𝔰𝔭₄^∨(1)) the augmented dual Selmer group vanishes.

nodes.title: Ordinary GSp₄ seed data (Hypothesis 6.3.1)
nodes.statement: Let p > 2 split completely in the totally real field F⁺, and identify the places v | ∞ and v | p through a fixed ı : ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_p. An ordinary GSp₄ seed datum consists of: an ordinary cuspidal automorphic representation π of GSp₄(𝔸_{F⁺}) with central character |·|² and weights ((k_v, l_v; 2))_{v|∞}, with its Galois representation ρ_{π,p} : G_{F⁺} → GSp₄(ℚ̄_p) (BCGP Theorem 1.8.17; AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity AP.0/weight-two-galois in parallel weight 2) and residual representation ρ̄ = ρ̄_{π,p}; a finite set R of finite places prime to p containing the prime-to-p places where π ramifies; for each v | p an ordinary p-stabilization (α_v, β_v) of ρ̄|G_{F⁺_v}; and a place w₀; such that: (1) ρ̄ is GSp₄-reasonable (OL.4/gsp4-reasonable), in particular absolutely irreducible; (2) ρ̄ is tidy (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7/vast-tidy-and-enormous-gsp4-subgroups); (3) for each v | p, ρ̄|G_{F⁺_v} is ordinary of weight 2 with p-stabilization (α_v, β_v) compatible with a fixed ordinary p-stabilization of π_v; (4) for each v | p, ρ_{π,p}|G_{F⁺_v}, viewed as a point of R^△_v (defined with (α_v, β_v)) through the chosen stabilization of π_v, lies on a unique irreducible component of Spec R^△_v (LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7/gsp4-ordinary-flag-incidence); (5) for each v ∈ R, ρ̄|G_{F⁺_v} is trivial, q_v ≡ 1 mod p (mod 9 if p = 3) and π_v^{Iw(v)} ≠ 0; (6) w₀ is an unramified place of residue characteristic > 5 with q_{w₀} ≢ 1 mod p such that no two eigenvalues of ρ̄(Frob_{w₀}) have ratio q_{w₀} (it exists because ρ̄ is tidy). Put S = S_p ∪ R ∪ {w₀}. The weights need not be parallel weight 2.
proofSteps: Collect the hypotheses of BCGP Hypothesis 6.3.1 as fields. For w₀: tidiness gives h ∈ ρ̄(G_{F⁺}) with ν(h) ≠ 1 such that no two eigenvalues of h (not necessarily distinct) have ratio ν(h); Chebotarev gives infinitely many unramified w₀ of residue characteristic > 5 with ρ̄(Frob_{w₀}) conjugate to h. As ν ∘ ρ̄ = ε̄^{−1}, ν(h) is q_{w₀} or q_{w₀}^{−1} in k (according to the Frobenius convention), and the set of eigenvalue ratios is stable under inversion; so q_{w₀} ≢ 1 mod p and no ratio equals q_{w₀}.
Condition (6) makes H⁰(G_{F⁺_{w₀}}, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) = 0, so the lifting ring at w₀ is formally smooth over O and the level at w₀ can be taken neat (BCGP21 §7.8 as BCGP cite it).
acceptance: Every seed datum puts ρ̄ in the situation of BCGP21 Hypothesis 7.8.1 except possibly for residual p-distinguishedness.

nodes.title: The selected ordinary problems S_1 and S_{1,π}
nodes.statement: Let (π, (α_v, β_v), R, w₀) be an ordinary GSp₄ seed datum (OL.4/ordinary-seed-datum) with S = S_p ∪ R ∪ {w₀}. For v | p let D^△_v be the ordinary problem of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7/gsp4-ordinary-flag-incidence over Λ_{GSp₄,v} = O⟦(O^×_{F⁺_v}(p))²⟧, taking the unramified characters χ_1, χ_2 with χ_1(Frob_v) = α_v and χ_2(Frob_v) = β_v; for v ∈ R let D^1_v be the problem of unipotently ramified lifts (LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2/gsp4-ihara-avoidance-rings with trivial characters); D^□_{w₀} all lifts. Then S_1 = (ρ̄, S, {Λ_{GSp₄,v}}_{v∈S_p} ∪ {O}_{v∈S∖S_p}, {D^△_v}_{v∈S_p} ∪ {D^1_v}_{v∈R} ∪ {D^□_{w₀}}), a GSp₄ problem over Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺} = ⊗̂_{v|p} Λ_{GSp₄,v}. For v | p let R^{△,π}_v be the quotient of R^△_v by the minimal prime of the unique component through ρ_{π,p}|G_{F⁺_v} (seed condition (4)), and D^{△,π}_v its problem; S_{1,π} replaces D^△_v by D^{△,π}_v. There is a surjection R_{S_1} ↠ R_{S_{1,π}} of Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}-algebras, and when ρ̄ is residually p-distinguished D^△_v is the problem D^{B,α_v}_v of BCGP21.
proofSteps: The local problems are Ĝsp₄-stable and representable, so S_1 and S_{1,π} are GSp₄ problems.
Restricting the selected component is well defined because of seed condition (4).
In the residually p-distinguished case the flag is unique and G_v → Spec R^□_v is a closed immersion, so D^△_v is the B-ordinary problem (L7/gsp4-borel-ordinary-conditions).
acceptance: ρ_{π,p} with its stabilizations is a Q̄_p-point of R_{S_{1,π}}.

nodes.title: The Galois representation over the GSp₄ Hida–Hecke algebra with the flag-image condition
nodes.statement: In the setting of OL.4/selected-ordinary-problem, let M^1 be the finite free Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}-module obtained from the ordinary part of the coherent H⁰ of Hilbert–Siegel Shimura varieties (BCGP21 §7.8–7.9 with I = ∅; AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity AP.1/hecke-modules), and T_{S_1} the Hida–Hecke algebra acting faithfully on it. There is a continuous ρ : G_{F⁺} → GSp₄(T_{S_1}) of type S_1, unique up to strict equivalence, whose characteristic polynomials of Frobenius at v ∉ S are the Hecke polynomials Q_v(X), giving a surjection R_{S_1} ↠ T_{S_1} of Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}-algebras; the same holds with Taylor–Wiles data Q, compatibly with Δ_Q. Put T_{S_{1,π}} = R_{S_{1,π}} ⊗_{R_{S_1}} T_{S_1}.
proofSteps: Follow BCGP21 Theorem 7.9.4 (AP.2/hida-hecke-galois) as generalised by Whitmore Theorem 7.8: embed T_{S_1} into the ring A of tuples (a, (a_π)) ⊂ k × ∏_π O_{E_π} indexed by classical ordinary π of large regular weight contributing to M^1, glue the Galois representations ρ_π, and pass to Artinian quotients.

The flag-image condition D^△_v is defined as a scheme-theoretic image and is not understood on general Artinian rings; but since T_{S_1} is reduced, O-flat and embeds in ∏_π O_{E_π}, a map R^□_v → T_{S_1} factors through R^△_v as soon as each composite R^□_v → O_{E_π} does, that is as soon as each ρ_π|G_{F⁺_v} is ordinary with stabilization lifting (α_v, β_v); this is BCGP's remark that only the O_{E′}-points of D^△_v are used.
At R the unipotent condition and at Taylor–Wiles places the Δ_Q-action follow as in Whitmore Theorem 7.7 and BCGP21 Theorem 7.9.4.
acceptance: T_{S_1} is finite over Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}, since it acts faithfully on the finite free module M^1.

sources.match: States that the constructions of BCGP21 §7.8 and Whitmore §7 go through with D^△_v, since the proof of Whitmore's Theorem 7.8 (generalizing BCGP21 Theorem 7.9.4) uses only the O_{E′}-points of D^△_v; there is a surjection R_{S_1} → T_{S_1} onto the Hida–Hecke algebra acting faithfully on a finite free Λ-module from ordinary coherent H⁰.

Constructs the Galois representation over the Hida–Hecke algebra with Taylor–Wiles data by embedding the Hecke algebra in a product of rings of integers indexed by classical ordinary forms of large weight and gluing.

nodes.title: The automorphic ordinary component dominates the local weight space
nodes.statement: Let p > 2 split completely in the totally real field F⁺, and let (π, (α_v, β_v)_{v|p}, R, w₀) be an ordinary GSp₄ seed datum (OL.4/ordinary-seed-datum) with residual representation ρ̄ = ρ̄_{π,p} and S = S_p ∪ R ∪ {w₀}; let S_{1,π} be the selected problem, R_{S_{1,π}} its deformation ring and T_{S_{1,π}} = R_{S_{1,π}} ⊗_{R_{S_1}} T_{S_1} (OL.4/selected-ordinary-problem, OL.4/gsp4-hida-galois-representation), Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺} = ⊗̂_{v|p} Λ_{GSp₄,v}. For every v | p the composite Spec R^{△,π}_v → Spec Λ_{GSp₄,v} is surjective. Consequently there is a minimal prime of R^{△,π}_v/(p) (viewed in R^△_v/(p)) containing the minimal prime of R^{△,π}_v and no other minimal prime of R^△_v, and R^{△,π}_v has relative dimension 16 over O.
proofSteps: Let Q_π ⊂ T_{S_1} be a minimal prime contained in the prime of π (with its stabilizations). The composite R^△_v → R_{S_1} → T_{S_1} → T_{S_1}/Q_π factors through R^{△,π}_v by seed condition (4).

The composite Spec T_{S_1}/Q_π → Spec R^{△,π}_v → Spec Λ_{GSp₄,v} equals Spec T_{S_1}/Q_π → Spec Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺} → Spec Λ_{GSp₄,v}. The second map is surjective; the first is surjective because T_{S_1}/Q_π is finite and torsion-free over the domain Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺} ≅ O⟦x_1, …, x_{2[F⁺:ℚ]}⟧ (p > 2), T_{S_1} acting faithfully on the finite free module M^1.

Hence Spec R^{△,π}_v → Spec Λ_{GSp₄,v} is surjective, which is the hypothesis of BCGP Lemma 6.2.6 (LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7/gsp4-ordinary-weight-two-components (2)), whose conclusion is the second sentence.
acceptance: The hypothesis of Lemma 6.2.6 is checked globally, not by a local analysis of R^△_v.

nodes.title: Patched Hida modules for the selected problem
nodes.statement: Let p > 2 split completely in the totally real field F⁺, and let (π, (α_v, β_v)_{v|p}, R, w₀) be an ordinary GSp₄ seed datum (OL.4/ordinary-seed-datum) with residual representation ρ̄ = ρ̄_{π,p} and S = S_p ∪ R ∪ {w₀}; let S_{1,π} be the selected problem, R_{S_{1,π}} its deformation ring and T_{S_{1,π}} = R_{S_{1,π}} ⊗_{R_{S_1}} T_{S_1} (OL.4/selected-ordinary-problem, OL.4/gsp4-hida-galois-representation), Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺} = ⊗̂_{v|p} Λ_{GSp₄,v}. Enlarge E to contain μ_p (μ_9 if p = 3) and fix, for v ∈ R, characters χ_v = (χ_{v,1}, χ_{v,2}) nontrivial and trivial mod λ with χ_{v,1} ≠ χ_{v,2}^{±1}; let S_χ be S_1 with D^{χ_v}_v in place of D^1_v. Let t and Taylor–Wiles data Q_N (N ≥ 1) be as in Whitmore Lemma 7.10, built from OL.4/reasonable-taylor-wiles-places, Δ_∞ ↠ Δ_{Q_N}, and S_∞ = 𝒯⟦Δ_∞⟧ with 𝒯 the framing ring over Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺} (OL.4/gsp4-lambda-deformation-problem) and augmentation ideal a_∞. Let R^1_∞, R^χ_∞ be power series rings in g = t − 4[F⁺:ℚ] + #S − 1 variables over R^loc_{S_1,S}, R^loc_{S_χ,S}, and R_{∞,π} = R^1_∞ ⊗_{R^loc_{S_1,S}} R^loc_{S_{1,π},S}. The patching data are: Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}-algebra maps S_∞ → R^1_∞ → R_{S_1} and S_∞ → R^χ_∞ → R_{S_χ}; finite S_∞-modules M^1_∞ and M^χ_∞, free over S_∞, with M^·_∞/a_∞ ≅ M^· (the Hida modules of OL.4/gsp4-hida-galois-representation); actions R^·_∞ → End_{S_∞}(M^·_∞) compatible with the actions of R_{S_·} on M^·; and identifications M^1_∞/λ ≅ M^χ_∞/λ compatible with R^1_∞/λ ≅ R^χ_∞/λ. Moreover M^·_∞ is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over R^·_∞, and dim (R^·_∞)′ = dim S_∞, where ′ is the maximal O-flat quotient.
proofSteps: Taylor–Wiles data: OL.4/reasonable-taylor-wiles-places applied to S_1 gives, for each N, data Q_N of level N with #Q_N = t and vanishing augmented dual Selmer group (Whitmore Lemma 7.10), with Whitmore's local conditions at Q_N.

Hecke side: the modules M^{·,Q_N} are finite free over Λ[Δ_{Q_N}] with Δ_{Q_N}-coinvariants M^· (Whitmore Propositions 7.5–7.6, the analogues of BCGP21 Proposition 7.9.8; AP.2/taylor-wiles-descent), and OL.4/gsp4-hida-galois-representation gives the Galois representations compatibly with Δ_{Q_N}.

Apply the patching criterion of BCGP21 Proposition 7.10.1 (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5/balanced-modules-and-module-patching, with zero defect since I = ∅) as in AP.3/patching-datum, with D^△_v in place of D^{B,α_v}_v; this is Whitmore Proposition 7.11 with I = ∅.

Dimensions: S_∞ is formally smooth over Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺} of relative dimension t + 11#S − 1, and (R^·_∞)′ is equidimensional of relative dimension g + 10#S + 4[F⁺:ℚ] over Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺} (relative dimension 16 over O above p, that is 14 over Λ_{GSp₄,v}, from L7/gsp4-ordinary-regularity, and 10 over O at R and at w₀ from R08.2/gsp4-ihara-avoidance-rings and LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1/smooth-points-generic-fibre); with g = t − 4[F⁺:ℚ] + #S − 1 these agree, so M^·_∞, being free over S_∞, is maximal Cohen–Macaulay (as in AP.3/patched-mcm).
acceptance: dim (R^1_∞)′ = dim (R^χ_∞)′ = dim S_∞.
M^1_∞ is free over S_∞ (no defect, since I = ∅).

nodes.title: The symplectic ordinary reduced R = T theorem for p > 2 (Theorem 6.3.4)
nodes.statement: Let p > 2 split completely in the totally real field F⁺, and let (π, (α_v, β_v)_{v|p}, R, w₀) be an ordinary GSp₄ seed datum (OL.4/ordinary-seed-datum) with residual representation ρ̄ = ρ̄_{π,p} and S = S_p ∪ R ∪ {w₀}; let S_{1,π} be the selected problem, R_{S_{1,π}} its deformation ring and T_{S_{1,π}} = R_{S_{1,π}} ⊗_{R_{S_1}} T_{S_1} (OL.4/selected-ordinary-problem, OL.4/gsp4-hida-galois-representation), Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺} = ⊗̂_{v|p} Λ_{GSp₄,v}. Then the map R_{S_{1,π}} → T_{S_{1,π}} has nilpotent kernel, so (R_{S_{1,π}})_red ≅ T_{S_{1,π}}: R = T holds, up to nilpotents, on exactly the chosen local components above p.
proofSteps: It suffices to show that the support of M^1 in Spec R_{S_1} contains Spec R_{S_1,π}, hence that the support of M^1_∞ contains every irreducible component of Spec R_{∞,π}.

Ihara avoidance (Taylor), exactly as in OL.3/ihara-avoidance-support: on the χ-side the local rings at R are irreducible (R08.2/gsp4-ihara-avoidance-rings (1)), so after enlarging E the selected χ-ring R^χ_{∞,π} is irreducible; M^χ_∞ is nonzero there, since M^χ_∞/λ ≅ M^1_∞/λ and the latter is nonzero; so M^χ_∞ has full support on Spec R^χ_{∞,π}, and reducing modulo λ (R^χ_∞/λ ≅ R^1_∞/λ) shows that the support of M^1_∞/λ contains Spec R_{∞,π}/λ (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P9/support-transport-avoiding-ihara for the transport of support).

Every component of the support of M^1_∞ and every component of Spec R_{∞,π} has dimension dim S_∞; so M^1_∞ is supported on a component of R_{∞,π} as soon as it is supported at a point lying on that component alone.

Such points exist in the special fibre for each factor: above p by OL.5/component-dominance and Lemma 6.2.6 (L7/gsp4-ordinary-weight-two-components (2)); at R by BCGP21 Proposition 7.4.7 (R08.2/gsp4-ihara-avoidance-rings (2)); at w₀ because R^□_{w₀} is formally smooth by the choice of w₀ (R08.1/smooth-points-generic-fibre (1)). Products of such points work for the completed tensor product.

nodes.title: Finiteness of the selected symplectic ordinary deformation ring
nodes.statement: Let p > 2 split completely in the totally real field F⁺, and let (π, (α_v, β_v)_{v|p}, R, w₀) be an ordinary GSp₄ seed datum (OL.4/ordinary-seed-datum) with residual representation ρ̄ = ρ̄_{π,p} and S = S_p ∪ R ∪ {w₀}; let S_{1,π} be the selected problem, R_{S_{1,π}} its deformation ring and T_{S_{1,π}} = R_{S_{1,π}} ⊗_{R_{S_1}} T_{S_1} (OL.4/selected-ordinary-problem, OL.4/gsp4-hida-galois-representation), Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺} = ⊗̂_{v|p} Λ_{GSp₄,v}. Then R_{S_{1,π}} is a finite Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}-algebra.
proofSteps: T_{S_1} is finite over Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}, acting faithfully on the finite free module M^1; so is its quotient T_{S_{1,π}}.

By OL.5/symplectic-ordinary-r-equals-t the kernel of R_{S_{1,π}} → T_{S_{1,π}} is nilpotent, so R_{S_{1,π}}/m_Λ R_{S_{1,π}} has finite length and R_{S_{1,π}} is finite over Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺} (R03.4/finiteness-of-deformation-rings-criteria).
acceptance: Finiteness is what Proposition 7.5.10 uses at p > 2: for a minimal prime Q of R_S through ρ, R_{S_1}/Q factors through R_{S_{1,π}} and is finite over Λ_{GSp₄,ℚ}.

Whitmore's local deformation problem at Taylor–Wiles places with semisimple (not necessarily regular) Frobenius, for Ĝ = GSp₄ with fixed similitude and p ≥ 3 (Whitmore, arXiv:2205.05062v3, §3.1, the problem D^TW_v attached to the Levi subgroup M_ḡ centralizing ḡ_v = ρ̄(Frob_v), with q_v ≡ 1 mod p^n): representability and formal smoothness over O[Δ_v], Δ_v the p-part of the k(v)-points of the centre of M_ḡ; the Selmer condition L_v = H¹_ur(F_v, 𝔰𝔭₄) + H¹(F_v, N_v), N_v = Lie Z(M_ḡ) ∩ 𝔰𝔭₄ (Whitmore (3.1)); and the dual condition H¹_ur(F_v, N_v^∨(1)) (Whitmore Lemma 3.14).
